sources.entry: Middleware - Tool designed to help engineering leaders measure and analyze the effectiveness of their teams using the DORA metrics. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker/Python/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Middleware is an open-source tool that helps engineering leaders measure and analyze team effectiveness using the DORA metrics.
summary.what_it_does: Middleware is a self-hosted engineering management tool that calculates the four DORA metrics (Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Mean Time to Restore, Change Failure Rate) for teams. According to the README, it can display DORA metrics using only Pull Request data from Git, and it also draws on Deployments and Incidents. Users generate a personal access token from their code provider, create a team, select repositories for that team, and then view DORA metrics. Settings cover incident filters, excluded pull requests, and production branches. The README also lists CI/CD tool integration, visualization of KPIs, customizable reports and dashboards, and integration with project management platforms as features. The app runs as separate analytics and sync servers alongside a web frontend, backed by Postgres and Redis.
use_cases: track deployment frequency and lead time for changes
monitor mean time to restore after incidents
calculate change failure rate from pull requests
build DORA metrics dashboards for engineering managers
how_to_run: Ensure Docker is installed and running.
docker logs -f middleware (then wait for services to start)
notable: Calculates DORA metrics from Pull Request data alone, without requiring other integrations
Ships as a single Docker image with analytics server, sync server, and web app
Includes dev.sh script for Docker-based development with docker compose watch
Includes a developer automation script (make_new_setting.py) to scaffold new backend settings
Gitpod support for running in a remote workspace
caveats: README recommends at least 16GB RAM for local development
Manual setup requires Python 3.11.6, Node.js 22, Postgres and Redis configured separately
